title_en: Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Intellectual Property Civil Litigation

articles.content_en: Article 1 Parties to a civil action involving intellectual property shall follow the principle of good faith and actively, comprehensively, correctly, and honestly provide evidence in accordance with the provisions of laws and judicial interpretations.

Article 2 A party shall provide evidence to prove the claims it raises. Based on the circumstances of the case, the People's Court may apply the provisions of Article 65, paragraph 2 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, and require the party to provide relevant evidence taking into account the party's claims and the facts to be proved, the party's possession of evidence, and its capacity to adduce evidence.

Article 4 Where the defendant claims a lawful source defense in accordance with law, it shall adduce evidence to prove the fact that the accused infringing product or reproduction was lawfully obtained, including a lawful purchase channel, a reasonable price, and a direct supplier, etc.
If the evidence of the source of the accused infringing product or reproduction provided by the defendant is consistent with the degree of its reasonable duty of care, it may be determined that the defendant has completed the adduction of evidence referred to in the preceding paragraph, and it shall be presumed that the defendant did not know that the accused infringing product or reproduction infringed intellectual property rights. The defendant's business scale, degree of professionalism, market trading practices, etc., may be used as evidence to determine its reasonable duty of care.

Article 6 For the basic facts found in an administrative act for which no administrative action has been initiated within the statutory time limit, or for the part of the basic facts found in an administrative act that have been confirmed by an effective judgment, the parties in a civil action involving intellectual property need not prove them again, unless there is contrary evidence sufficient to overturn them.

Article 7 The physical objects, invoices, etc. obtained by a right holder, either by itself or through another person, from purchasing infringing items from the accused infringer in the name of an ordinary purchaser for the purpose of discovering or proving intellectual property infringement may be used as evidence to initiate a lawsuit against the accused infringer for infringement.
Evidence formed by the accused infringer's implementation of intellectual property infringement based on the conduct of others may be used as evidence for the right holder to sue it for infringement, except where the accused infringer only implemented the intellectual property infringement based solely on the right holder's evidence-gathering conduct.

Article 9 Where evidence formed outside the territory of the People's Republic of China falls under any of the following circumstances, and a party raises an objection solely on the ground that the evidence has not undergone authentication formalities, the People's Court shall not uphold such objection:
(1) the party raising the objection expressly acknowledges the authenticity of the evidence;
(2) the opposing party provides witness testimony confirming the authenticity of the evidence, and the witness explicitly states that it would be willing to accept punishment if the testimony is false.
If the witness's false testimony referred to in item (2) of the preceding paragraph constitutes a circumstance under Article 111 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall handle it in accordance with law.

Article 10 If the formalities of notarization, authentication, or other certification have been completed for the power of attorney in accordance with the provisions of Articles 59 and 264 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China in the first-instance proceedings, the People's Court may not require the said certification formalities for the power of attorney to be completed again in subsequent proceedings.

Article 12 The People's Court, when taking evidence preservation, shall limit itself to effectively fixing the evidence and shall minimize damage to the value of the subject matter of preservation and the impact on the normal production and operation of the evidence holder.
If the evidence preservation involves a technical solution, preservation measures such as making an on-site inspection record, drawings, photographs, audio recordings, video recordings, copying design and production drawings, etc., may be taken.

Article 13 If a party, without justifiable reasons, refuses to cooperate with or obstructs evidence preservation, resulting in the inability to preserve evidence, the People's Court may determine that such party shall bear adverse consequences. If the circumstances constitute those under Article 111 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall handle it in accordance with law.

Article 14 Where a party, without authorization, dismantles the physical evidence, alters the evidentiary materials, or commits other acts that damage evidence that has already been preserved by the People's Court, rendering the evidence unusable, the People's Court may determine that such party shall bear adverse consequences. If the circumstances constitute those under Article 111 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall handle it in accordance with law.

Article 15 The People's Court may, when taking evidence preservation, require the parties or litigation agents to be present, and may, when necessary, notify a person with specialized knowledge to be present upon the application of a party, and may also appoint a technical investigation officer to participate in the evidence preservation.
If the evidence is held by a person not involved in the case, the People's Court may take preservation measures against the evidence held by such person.

Article 16 The People's Court, when taking evidence preservation, shall make a record and a list of preserved evidence, recording the time and place of preservation, the persons executing the preservation, the persons present, the process of preservation, and the status of the subject matter of preservation, and shall have the persons executing the preservation and the persons present sign or affix their seals. If the relevant persons refuse to sign or affix their seals, the validity of the preservation shall not be affected, and the People's Court may note this on the record and take photographs or video recordings.

Article 17 If the respondent raises an objection to the scope, measures, necessity, etc. of the evidence preservation and provides relevant evidence, and the People's Court, upon examination, finds that the grounds for the objection are established, it may modify, terminate, or discharge the evidence preservation.

Article 18 If the applicant waives the use of the preserved evidence, but the preserved evidence involves the ascertainment of the basic facts of the case or other parties claim to use it, the People's Court may examine and determine such evidence.

Article 20 With the permission of the People's Court or the consent of both parties, the expert evaluator may entrust the testing of part of the issues involved in the evaluation to another testing institution, and the expert evaluator shall bear legal liability for the expert opinion issued based on the testing results.

Article 21 If the field of expert evaluation business does not have a unified registration and management system for expert evaluators and expert evaluation institutions, the People's Court may determine a professional institution or professional with corresponding technical expertise to conduct the evaluation in accordance with the procedure for selecting expert evaluators prescribed in Article 32 of the Several Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Evidence in Civil Litigation.

Article 22 The People's Court shall hear the opinions of all parties and determine the scope of evaluation in light of the evidence submitted by the parties. During the evaluation process, if one party applies to change the scope of evaluation and the opposing party has no objection, the People's Court may grant the application.

Article 24 If a party bearing the burden of adducing evidence applies in writing for the People's Court to order the opposing party in control of the evidence to submit it, and the grounds for the application are established, the People's Court shall make a ruling ordering the opposing party to submit the evidence.

Article 25 If the People's Court, in accordance with law, requires a party to submit relevant evidence, and the party, without justifiable reasons, refuses to submit it, submits false evidence, destroys evidence, or commits other acts that render the evidence unusable, the People's Court may presume that the claim of the opposing party concerning the matter to be proved by that evidence is established.
If a party commits any of the acts listed in the preceding paragraph and such acts constitute circumstances under Article 111 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, the People's Court shall handle it in accordance with law.

Article 26 If evidence involves trade secrets or other commercial information that needs to be kept confidential, the People's Court shall, before the relevant litigation participants access the evidence, require them to sign a confidentiality agreement or make a confidentiality commitment, or order them by ruling or other legal document not to disclose, use, or allow others to use the secret information accessed during the proceedings for any purpose other than the litigation of this case.
If a party applies to restrict the scope of persons who may access the evidence referred to in the preceding paragraph, and the People's Court, upon examination, finds it necessary, it shall grant the application.

Article 27 Witnesses shall testify in court and undergo questioning by adjudicators and parties.
If both parties agree and the People's Court permits, and the witness does not appear in court, the People's Court shall organize the parties to cross-examine the witness testimony.

Article 28 A party may apply for a person with specialized knowledge to appear in court to give opinions on professional issues. With the permission of the court, a party may question the person with specialized knowledge.

Article 29 If the People's Court appoints a technical investigation officer to participate in a pre-trial conference or court hearing, the technical investigation officer may question parties, litigation agents, persons with specialized knowledge, witnesses, expert evaluators, inspectors, etc., regarding the technical issues involved in the case.

Article 30 If a party raises an objection to a notarized document and provides contrary evidence sufficient to overturn it, the People's Court shall not admit that notarized document.
If the grounds for a party's objection to a notarized document are established, the People's Court may require the notary institution to issue an explanation or make corrections, and shall examine and determine the notarized document in conjunction with other relevant evidence.

Article 31 Financial books, accounting vouchers, sales contracts, delivery and receipt documents, annual reports of listed companies, prospectuses, records from websites or brochures, transaction data stored in equipment systems, commodity circulation data compiled by third-party platforms, evaluation reports, intellectual property license contracts, and records from market regulation, tax, and financial authorities provided by the parties may be used as evidence to prove the amount of damages for intellectual property infringement claimed by the parties.

Article 33 These Provisions shall come into force on November 18, 2020. Where any relevant judicial interpretation previously issued by this Court is inconsistent with these Provisions, these Provisions shall prevail.
